summary: Berlin Mountain, Berkshire County, MA: 50-ft steel tower c.1915, staffed until 1923, moved to Brodie Mountain in Hancock; only footings remain on Berlin Mountain.

facts.status_note: Only footings remain on Berlin Mountain. The tower structure was moved to Brodie Mountain in Hancock in 1923; the Forest Lookouts page describes a new tubular steel tower there from 2009.

events.note: Built around 1915 by the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (Wikipedia); the register says first operated in 1915
First operated in 1915 per the register
Moved to Brodie Mountain in Hancock in late 1923, after New York's 1922 stations (Wikipedia); the Forest Lookouts page says the tower structure was moved there
Newspaper quoted on Forest Lookouts: the previously abandoned Brodie Mountain tower would return to service. In April 1954 it was still out of service.
A 50-foot tower was built at Brodie Mountain; the page does not say whether it reused the Berlin structure
A new tubular steel tower was erected at Brodie Mountain

corrections.why: The tower structure was moved to Brodie Mountain in 1923; only footings remain on Berlin Mountain. Current condition at Brodie is not confirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the site's elevation as 2,978 ft (908 m); Wikipedia gives the peak 2,818 ft (859 m). The story reports both and does not reconcile them.
The register places the site in Berkshire County. Wikipedia says Berlin Mountain's summit lies on the New York side of the state line and the east side is in Williamstown. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The 1915 to 1923 Berlin history is supported by the register and Wikipedia. The Brodie history comes from the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes 1950s newspapers, and it does not say whether any 1915 steelwork survives in the 2009 tower, so today's condition at Brodie is unconfirmed. A Trailspotting post from September 2026, seen only as a search snippet and not read, says the Hancock tower recently fell out of service and now carries radio and microwave equipment; verify before adding to status_note. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Massachusetts Facebook post, also seen only as a snippet, says the tower was rebuilt at Brodie in 1923. That conflicts with the 'moved' wording and was not cited. Access at either site is not described in the sources read.
